title: Cancel a Google Play Subscription on Android or Web (2026)
metaDescription: Cancel any Google Play subscription on Android or play.google.com. Uninstalling the app does not stop billing. Learn the steps and India UPI Autopay notes.
h1: How do I cancel a subscription that is billed through Google Play?
summary: On Android, open Google Play, go to your subscriptions under your profile, tap the subscription and choose Cancel subscription. On a computer, go to play.google.com, select Subscriptions, click Manage on the subscription and choose Cancel subscription. Uninstalling the app does not cancel it, and after you cancel you keep access until the end of the billing period you have already paid for.
stepsHeading: Cancel a Google Play subscription on Android

steps.name: Open subscriptions in Google Play
steps.text: Open the Google Play Store app and tap your profile picture at the top right. Look for Payments & subscriptions, then Subscriptions. Google's help describes this as going to subscriptions in Google Play, and menu names can differ by version.

steps.name: Select the subscription
steps.text: Check that the Google Account shown is the one you subscribed with. If the subscription is missing, switch accounts, because it may sit on a different Google Account.

steps.name: Tap Cancel subscription
steps.text: Tap the subscription, then tap Cancel subscription. If the screen offers to pause the subscription instead, choose whether you want to pause or to carry on with cancelling.

steps.name: Follow the instructions
steps.text: Follow the on-screen steps to finish. Then reopen the subscription to confirm it now shows as cancelled, with the date your access ends.

sections.heading: Uninstalling is not the same as cancelling
paragraphs: Google's help page is direct on this point: when you uninstall the app, your subscription does not cancel. The app disappears from your phone, but Google Play keeps billing you at the start of each billing cycle until you unsubscribe.

Uninstalling can be a separate step after you cancel. If an app is removed from Google Play, its future subscription is cancelled, and past subscriptions cannot be refunded except in the cases Google's refund policies cover.

sections.heading: Cancelling on a computer at play.google.com
paragraphs: Go to play.google.com and sign in to the Google Account that holds the subscription. Go to subscriptions in Google Play, find the subscription, click Manage, then click Cancel subscription and Continue.
Google's help says to sign in to the Google Account that has the subscriptions. If you cannot find it, it may be on a different Google Account, so switch accounts and check again.

sections.heading: What you keep after you cancel
paragraphs: When you cancel, you can keep using the subscription for the time you have already paid for. Google gives an example: a one-year subscription bought on 1 January and cancelled on 1 July keeps access until 31 December, and is not charged again the following 1 January.

Prepaid plans work differently. They expire at the end of their billing period, so you do not need to cancel them. If an unused prepaid plan is still in your account, you can request a refund under Google Play's refund rules.

Some apps offer a pause instead. Pausing takes effect at the end of the current billing period and can run from one week to three months, depending on the app. If you cancel a Play Pass subscription, apps you installed remain on your device, but in-app purchases are removed.

sections.heading: Restarting, refunds and failed payments
paragraphs: To restart a cancelled subscription, open subscriptions in Google Play, tap the subscription and choose Resubscribe. Some subscriptions cannot be resumed this way, and in that case you have to set up the subscription again.

Refunds are handled under Google Play's refund policies, and Google says past subscriptions cannot be refunded except in the cases its policy sets out. If a renewal payment fails, the subscription can be cancelled, so add a backup payment method to your Google Play account if you want to avoid interruptions.

sections.heading: Payment notes for India
paragraphs: Google Play's India page says that Netbanking has been discontinued as a payment method on Google Play from October 2025 until further notice. If your subscription was set up on Netbanking, add another payment method so the renewal does not fail.

UPI works on Google Play in India, and you can set up UPI Autopay for recurring subscriptions such as YouTube Premium or Google One. You manage the mandate in Google Pay: tap your profile picture, select Autopay, open the Live tab, tap the mandate, then choose Pause autopay or Cancel autopay. Cancel autopay asks for your UPI PIN.

Google Pay supports Autopay through certain UPI handles only. Google's page lists @okaxis, @okhdfcbank and @okicici, and explains how to create an additional UPI ID if yours ends in @oksbi. Cancelling the Play subscription and cancelling the mandate are separate steps, so check both.

sections.heading: How tracking renewals in Essara helps
paragraphs: Essara is a manual tracker. You add each Google Play subscription with its amount, billing cycle and next renewal date, and it shows the upcoming renewals with a reminder before each one. It cannot see the charge, because it does not connect to your Google Account, bank, UPI app or SMS.

faqs.q: Does uninstalling an app stop Google Play charges?
faqs.a: No. Google's help page says that when you uninstall the app, your subscription does not cancel, and you will keep being charged until you cancel it in Google Play.

faqs.q: Will I lose access as soon as I cancel a Google Play subscription?
faqs.a: Usually not. You keep access for the time you have already paid for, and the subscription ends at the end of the current billing period.

faqs.q: Can I pause a Google Play subscription instead of cancelling?
faqs.a: Only if the app allows it. When it does, the pause starts at the end of your current billing period and can last from one week to three months, depending on the app and subscription.

faqs.q: Why is my Google Play subscription cancelled after a failed payment?
faqs.a: If a payment is declined or has insufficient funds, the subscription may be cancelled. Google advises setting it up again, and adding a backup payment method so the next renewal does not fail.

faqs.q: How do I cancel a Google Play subscription from a computer?
faqs.a: Go to play.google.com, sign in to the right Google Account, go to subscriptions in Google Play, click Manage on the subscription, click Cancel subscription, select a reason and click Continue.
